content: Discussion for #Lean Pool > Announcements @ 💬 .

I guess this is also a challenge for me to write more challenges :-) Thanks for this! I have a much better idea of exactly what I will be needing for FLT and furthermore how to state it in Lean. I will still need to make some mathlib PRs before I can formalise some of the statements (in fact this is one of the bottlenecks -- missing definitions in mathlib) but I think it would be a very interesting idea if the community were to start filling them in.

FWIW I think Odlyzko is do-able and Mazur right now is a little out of reach because we are missing so many foundational definitions and API for them. There is ongoing work in Tau Ceti to try and get the elliptic curve and modular curve definitions up to speed.
A message was moved here from #Lean Pool > Announcements by Vasily Ilin.

The first challenge was solved in <24 hours. As @Kevin Buzzard pointed out, it's the easier of the two.
If anyone else has big standalone theorems they would like to pose as a challenge to formalize, please submit a challenge PR or message me your challenge statement.
Can you confirm that this solution did not use the recent proof of false which has spread like wildfire across many benchmarks? In other words, can you bump to 4.32.2?
Lean Pool is already on version 4.33-rc1. So it is unaffected by the kernel bug.

The community would love more challenges! From @Kevin Buzzard or others.
I just noticed that Lean Pool actually received two solutions to the Odlyzko challenge! The first one is already merged. The second one was a few hours behind.

I thought 4.33-rc1 is behind kernel bug fixes until we get 4.33-rc2. Did I understand it wrong?

Edit: Lean Web 4.33-rc1 still type-checks the exploit code

Vasily Ilin said:

The community would love more challenges!

What about LeanEval?

@Snir Broshi

What about LeanEval?

I do not understand your question. If you are asking for the difference between LeanEval and LeanPool's Challenges, they are completely different. LeanEval is an AI benchmark. LeanPool's Challenges is crowdsourced math formalization. But perhaps you are asking something else?

Both are hard math formalization challenges for people to solve which we would like to have.
Of course LeanEval allows private solutions, but since you're trying to get people to formalize useful stuff why not take most LeanEval challenges (with permission, of course)?
The purpose of "AI benchmark" seems irrelevant here, they have challenges and you want challenges, and it seems to fit your needs IIUC
Are you actually asking why not contaminate the most valuable benchmark that took the Lean community many months to build? And the only unsaturated benchmark.

I don't want challenges for the sake of boiling the ocean. I want theorems that are actually useful in real formalization projects to get formalized. E.g. Kevin always talks about how he assumes a bunch of pre 1980s results in his FLT project. Wouldn't it be nice if by the time he finished his part of the FLT, we crowdsourced all the pre-1980s, so that we'd have the complete FLT!

I'm not asking that, but I guess that's a possible counterargument. Though given that they already allow public solutions, I don't see how that's contaminating any more that it is already. If you were to post a LeanEval challenge to Lean Pool someone could formalize it, but they could just as well formalize it publicly and submit to LeanEval. I don't see the difference.

People should not be making their LeanEval solutions public. This contaminates the benchmark. I suppose it's not obvious to non-AI folks. Maybe @Kim Morrison can make this clarification somewhere on the LeanEval website.

It would be as if someone published all solutions to the PutnamBench in a repo. It would render the benchmark useless, which would be really bad, because without unsaturated benchmarks it's hard to know which AI models are better at lean

I understand the meaning of contamination, but you haven't responded to what I said at all.
Of course, you're free to ignore my suggestion, I just thought it was strangely missing from this thread/announcement (as opposed to you mentioning both TauCeti's roadmaps and formal-conjectures).

What is your suggestion? To take all LeanEval problems and make them challenges in Lean Pool? That would be a bad idea because it would contaminate the benchmark. It would also be a bad idea because the problems in Lean Eval were not chosen because they were necessary prerequisites in a real formalization project; they were chosen because they are hard
My suggestion was to consider where does LeanEval stand compared to Lean Pool challenges, as you did with the other similar efforts in the announcement.

Perhaps I need to take a step back and explain my vision for Lean Pool's challenges.

It's clear that AI is helpful in formalization. Right now people mostly use AI to formalize small-ish standalone results. This is nice, but it is not an organized process. For AI formalizations to become actually useful, the leaders of the Lean community need to tell the rest of us what would be useful. For example, Kevin is working on the FLT and has many examples of theorems that would be useful (Mazur's theorem being one example). LeanPool's Challenges is a way for the leaders to give specific results that are useful, and then people will formalize them in a crowdsourced way. The point is not to test AI, it's to actually formalize results that are useful in real formalization projects like the FLT.
